In terms of the shortness of its lifespan, however, I would disagree. A small website tends to run out of momentum slowly. Have a few less stories on the front page here and there, fewer people signing up. Slowly, slowly, slowly... and then you realize you haven't checked with it for a whole month, and most of the posts on the front page haven't budged in two months. So you have a zombie shambling forward. With more people, you get the distinct possibility of people trying to muscle their way in with political agendas and censorship in mind, but the lifespan of the community is longer.

That said, at least with the way Voat currently is, the chances are that anyone who tried to start screaming "safe space" would be downvoted into oblivion, if not basically pilloried freely. There are a lot of very, very angry reddit users here who are sick of political-correctness-or-else-doxtime in their face and are quite willing to make a very large fight of it.
